The test image shows a tomato stem at the soil line that has been cut open longitudinally. Key features:
- White cottony/mycelial material on the stem exterior at the soil line
- Bleached, pale cream interior pith tissue visible in the cut stem
- Plant is dead/collapsed with wilted brown leaves
- Infection clearly at/near soil level

This pattern strongly suggests either **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (white cotton-like mycelium, bleached hardened stem) or **Southern_Blight** (white mycelium at stem base). Let me view a reference for Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot.

The reference confirms Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot features: dense white cottony mycelium on stems with developing dark sclerotia.

Comparing to the test image:
- The test image shows a stem **cut open longitudinally** (exactly the diagnostic method described for Sclerotinia: "positive identification achieved by slicing the diseased stem longitudinally")
- White mycelial material is visible on the stem exterior at soil level
- The interior pith appears bleached/cream-colored (consistent with the "bleached and hardened" tissue description)
- The plant is collapsed/dead

This matches Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot strongly. Southern_Blight would show spherical mustard-seed-sized sclerotia and prominent surface mycelial mats on the soil; this image focuses on the cut stem interior typical of Sclerotinia diagnosis.
